text:
maria: quick heads-up — noticed a ~6% absolute drop in prefix-cache hit rate on the canary for model-gamma after deploy (canary-id: canary/2026-03-17-07). Trying to triage if this is a regression or workload shift.

aj: can you paste the canary id + the bench job id? also which commit?

maria: canary: canary/2026-03-17-07, bench: perf/kv-prefix/17861, commit: 9c4b2f3 (PR #3456). numbers: baseline hit 78.2% -> canary 72.1%. total tokens per-sec roughly same.

cheng: curious — PR #3456 touched prefetch and slot reclamation thresholds, could increase fragmentation. did you capture the prefix size histogram?

maria: not yet. I have the kvcache metrics exports + flamegraphs. uploading tarball to /home/maria/profiles/178612. link: https://internal.artifacts/reports/178612.tar.gz

samir: ops-bot also fired more eviction alerts during the canary window (spike at 07:12). @ops-bot can you post the alert id?

ops-bot: alert: kvcache_eviction_rate > 200/s for shard group sg-12 during 2026-03-17T07:10-07:20Z. id=alert-9092.

aj: thanks. i'll run the reproducer from perf/kv-prefix/17861 locally with the canary bundle. if it's fragmentation we should see an upward shift in small-fragment count + more evictions per MB.

cheng: here's a quick query you can run on the profiler VM — it prints prefix-length histogram and avg slots-per-prefix:

```
curl -sS http://profiler:9200/metrics/kvcache | jq '.prefix_lengths | to_entries | .[] | {len: .key, count: .value}'
```

maria: ran that, results are in the tarball under metrics/prefix_hist.json — small lengths (<=8B) increased 18%, and avg_slots_per_prefix from 1.9 -> 2.6.

aj: that avg_slots change smells like more fragmentation. can you grep for the reclamation/gc logs? look for "reclaim_slots" events around 07:10-07:20.

maria: found them: 9 lines with reclaim_slots=true and reclaimed=0 each. snippet:

```
[2026-03-17T07:11:03Z] shard=sg-12 reclaim_slots=true reclaimed=0 slots_free=0 reason=threshold
[2026-03-17T07:11:15Z] shard=sg-12 reclaim_slots=true reclaimed=0 slots_free=0 reason=threshold
```

samir: if reclamation is failing repeatedly, that will force more evictions. PR #3456 lowered the threshold to be more aggressive, but I guess if reclaim logic didn't adapt, it might just keep triggering without freeing contiguous space.

aj: can we repro with a targeted synthetic workload? maria, can you run perf/kv-prefix/17861 with \"--seed-frag-mode\" to stress small prefixes? I can run a debug build with extra logging for slot compaction.

maria: scheduling now, will post results in ~15m.

dev-bot: deploy canary/2026-03-17-07 rolled (commit 9c4b2f3) — CI: all green.

cheng: if the repro confirms fragmentation, plan A = revert the prefetch/reclaim tweaks from #3456, plan B = fix reclaim to compact across slot boundaries. favours revert for fast mitigation.

aj: agreed, but let's confirm with the repro before reverting. if maria's run reproduces, i'll open a hotfix PR to revert and include a small unit test that asserts reclaim frees contiguous slots under synthetic inserts.

maria: repro run attached: perf/kv-prefix/17861/attempt-2 — shows hit 71.9%, eviction_rate 215/s, reclaim_logs same pattern. uploading more logs to the tarball.

samir: i'll take ownership of creating the hotfix PR if we need it. tagging @aj for review. :white_check_mark:

aj: ping noted. i'll try to get an initial review in the next hour. maria — please keep the canary pinned so we can compare after revert.

maria: pinned. also started a longer trace capture for 1h to help root cause. will update thread when done.

cheng: also adding a small sampling job to perf infra to collect "slots per prefix" every 5m for the next day so we can see if this drifts in prod.

maria: thanks all. summary: repro indicates higher fragmentation + reclaim didn't free slots -> evictions up -> hit rate down. next: aj/revert PR if repro holds; samir will cut hotfix; cheng will add sampling; i'll keep the trace and artifact links in the tarball.

aj: acknowledged.
